title: Because, So or Although?
intro: Cause, result or contrast? Pick the linking word that fits what the sentence is doing.

A2.q: I stayed home ___ I was ill.
A2.why: Being ill is the reason I stayed home: because.

A2.q: It was raining, ___ we took an umbrella.
A2.why: Taking the umbrella is the result of the rain: so.

A2.q: ___ it was cold, we went for a walk.
A2.why: Cold weather and a walk are a surprise together: although for contrast.

A2.q: She was tired ___ she had worked all day.
A2.why: Working all day is the reason she was tired: because.

A2.q: He studied hard, ___ he passed the exam.
A2.why: Passing is the result of studying: so.

A2.q: ___ she was busy, she helped me.
A2.why: Busy, but she still helped: although for contrast.

A2.q: I was hungry, ___ I made a sandwich.
A2.why: The sandwich is the result of the hunger: so.

A2.q: We stayed inside ___ it was snowing.
A2.why: The snow is the reason we stayed in: because.

A2.q: ___ he was late, he missed the bus.
A2.why: Being late is the reason he missed the bus: because. So can't start this sentence.

A2.q: It was expensive, ___ we bought it anyway.
The cowboy was thirsty, ___ he went into the saloon.
A2.why: Going into the saloon is the result of his thirst: so.

A2.q: ___ it was a sunny Sunday, the beach in Valencia was almost empty.
A2.why: Sun on a Sunday but an empty beach is a surprise: although.

B1.q: ___ the traffic, we arrived on time.
B1.why: Before a noun (“the traffic”) we need despite. Although needs a full clause.

B1.q: ___ he trained every day, he didn't win.
B1.why: Training but not winning is a surprise: even though for strong contrast.

B1.q: She left early ___ she had a meeting.
B1.why: The meeting is the reason: since means because here.

B1.q: ___ being tired, she finished the report.
B1.why: Despite goes before an -ing form: tired, but she still finished.

B1.q: ___ it was late, we decided to leave.
B1.why: The late hour is the reason: as means because here.

B1.q: He passed the exam ___ he barely studied.
B1.why: “Barely studied” and passing is a surprise: even though.

B1.q: ___ the bad weather, the match continued.
B1.why: Before a noun we need in spite of. Although needs a subject and verb.

B1.q: I couldn't sleep ___ the noise outside.
B1.why: The noise (a noun) is the reason: because of. “Despite of” doesn't exist.

B1.q: ___ she apologised, he was still angry.
B1.why: “She apologised” is a full clause, so we need although, not despite.

B1.q: We took a taxi ___ we were in a hurry.
B1.why: Being in a hurry is the reason: since means because here.

B1.q: ___ the heat, the farmers worked in the rice fields all afternoon.
B1.why: Heat but hard work: contrast before a noun, so in spite of.

B1.q: Dr Jenner became famous ___ he found a way to stop smallpox.
B1.why: His discovery is the reason for his fame: because + a full clause.

B2.q: The flight was delayed ___ bad weather.
B2.why: The bad weather (a noun) is the cause: due to.

B2.q: ___ his lack of experience, he got the job.
B2.why: No experience but he got the job: contrast before a noun, despite.

B2.q: He is quiet, ___ his brother is very outgoing.
B2.why: Two people compared side by side: whereas.

B2.q: The show was cancelled ___ low ticket sales.
B2.why: Low sales (a noun) are the cause: owing to.

B2.q: ___ she disagreed, she signed the contract.
B2.why: “She disagreed” is a full clause in contrast: although.

B2.q: He failed the exam; ___, he didn't give up.
B2.why: After a semicolon, a contrast word with a comma: nevertheless.

B2.q: ___ that the roads were icy, they cancelled the trip.
B2.why: “Given that” introduces a reason we all know: icy roads.

B2.q: Sales rose in Asia, ___ they fell in Europe.
B2.why: Two places compared, one up and one down: whereas.
Poor planning (a noun) is the cause: due to.
Albeit adds a small contrast without a verb: passed, but only just.

B2.q: Tombstone grew fast ___ the discovery of silver nearby.
B2.why: The silver (a noun phrase) is the cause: owing to.

B2.q: Valencia is hot and humid in summer, ___ Madrid is hot and dry.
B2.why: Two cities compared side by side: whereas.

C1.q: The event went ahead ___ the storm.
C1.why: Notwithstanding is a formal despite: the storm didn't stop it.
Albeit + an adverb adds a small contrast with no verb.

C1.q: ___ his objections, the plan was approved.
C1.why: Objections but approval: notwithstanding, a formal despite, before a noun.

C1.q: The rule applies ___ it doesn't conflict with local law.
C1.why: Insofar as means “to the extent that”: it sets a limit.

C1.q: She resigned ___ growing pressure from the board.
C1.why: The pressure (a noun) is the cause: on account of.

C1.q: It was a small victory, ___ an important one.
C1.why: Albeit + a noun phrase: small, but still important.

C1.q: ___ the risks, the board approved the merger.
C1.why: Risks but approval: notwithstanding for a formal contrast.

C1.q: The strategy worked, ___ only in the short term.
C1.why: Albeit adds a limit without a verb: it worked, but only briefly.

C1.q: He was promoted ___ his outstanding results.
C1.why: His results (a noun phrase) are the reason: on account of.

C1.q: The theory holds true ___ conditions remain stable.
C1.why: Insofar as sets the condition: true only to that extent.

C1.q: The surgeon carried on with the operation, ___ the lack of anaesthetic.
C1.why: No anaesthetic but he carried on: notwithstanding, a formal despite.

C1.q: The new law was popular in Valencia, ___ less so in Alicante.
C1.why: Albeit works without a verb. Whereas would need a full clause.
